data.headline: You have the right to remain silent
data.subheadline: And you should use it more than you think

data.title: When to Actually Stay Silent
items: Police ask: 'Do you know why I stopped you?'
data.footnote: Source: ACLU Know Your Rights Guide

data.myth: Only guilty people refuse to answer police questions
data.fact: The Fifth Amendment protects everyone. Innocent people get convicted from misinterpreted statements daily.
data.proof: According to the Innocence Project, false confessions contribute to 29% of wrongful convictions

data.callToAction: Did you know about this right?

manifest.caption:
Police officer: 'Do you know why I stopped you?'

You: 'I'd prefer not to answer questions.'

That's it.

You're not being rude.

You're exercising your Fifth Amendment right.

Know your rights. Use them.

sourceArticle.title: Your Right to Remain Silent: What You Need to Know
